A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FlashMask. All pages, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison. The existing material can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A report original training throughput, convergence, memory consumption, sparsity experiments, and attention-kernel benchmarks.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, and Appendix B adds FlashInfer comparisons and mask-block-size measurements in Tables 10–14.

M1.justification: The four-vector mask representation, min/max preprocessing, block-skipping procedure, and forward/backward Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. Appendix B evaluates the existing method without introducing an inference-specific algorithm.

E1.justification: Although framed as inference evaluation, Appendix B reuses Appendix A.5.2's synthetic data, existing Causal Document, Document, and Shared Question masks, and existing sequence lengths. Forward attention was already benchmarked; the additions concern comparators and execution settings rather than new data domains or task requirements.

E2.justification: Appendix B adds FlashInfer 0.1.6 as a comparator through its DenseMask and SparseMask implementations. The existing comparisons with Vanilla Attention, FlashAttention DenseMask, and FlexAttention remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds a forward-only protocol with batch size 1, 32 query heads, 8 key/value heads, head dimension 128, and sub-document lengths divisible by 64. It also varies sparse-mask block size. These are additional settings, not revisions to the retained training and FlexAttention protocols.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a focused sensitivity analysis of FlashInfer's sparse-mask block size, with settings labeled R/C from 1 to 64 at three sequence lengths. Tables 12–14 reveal configuration-dependent rankings. Existing convergence, sparsity, and memory analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A retains the same timing averages over 100 kernel runs following 10 warm-up iterations. Appendix B adds point estimates without new seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Tables 10–14 add a substantial comparative result set while existing results remain unchanged. At 32K, Table 10 reports FlashMask at 137.09 TFLOPs/s versus FlashInfer SparseMask at 15.01. Conversely, Table 13 reports SparseMask at 185.16 for R/C=64 versus FlashMask at 139.84. These are newly reported comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The mask definitions, block-classification equations, complexity analysis, and correctness reasoning in Sections 3–4 are unchanged. Appendix B adds empirical evaluation and implementation discussion, not new mathematical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about mask expressiveness, linear mask memory, computational exactness, training speedups, and performance against FlexAttention. The new inference discussion remains in Appendix B.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds explanations involving redundant dense-mask computation and padding overhead for small sparse blocks, and argues that large blocks are seldom practical. Its claim of consistent superiority conflicts with the larger-block results in Tables 12–14. Section 6's existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B documents FlashInfer 0.1.6, CUDA 12.1, PyTorch 2.4, the A100-SXM 80G environment, the two comparator APIs, and block-aligned data preparation. It also supplies a versioned source-code locator. Existing implementation details and PaddlePaddle/PaddleNLP access information remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Ye et al. (2025) FlashInfer reference and positions FlashMask against this inference attention implementation in Appendix B. The existing related-work discussion and references otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 appends an inference section with setup, comparison, and block-size subsections, adds acknowledgments, and introduces the ICLR 2025 publication header. The existing scientific prose and section organization are essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 10–14 add displays of forward performance and block-size sensitivity. Existing figures and table contents are retained, with some appendix text and table placement shifting through reflow. There is no substantial redesign of the existing presentation.

improvement.justification: Appendix B modestly strengthens the evidence through a relevant additional comparator, documented settings, and a sensitivity analysis that exposes configuration-dependent performance. The original scientific content is preserved. The benefit is limited by overstated interpretation: B.2 claims consistent superiority, although Tables 12–14 show FlashInfer SparseMask outperforming FlashMask at larger blocks. The added measurements are useful, but their conclusions require qualification.
